title: Azure Event Grid Overview
description: Understand how Event Grid delivers events from Azure services to your handlers in real time.

data.text: Azure Event Grid is a fully managed event routing service. It lets you build event-driven applications by reacting to events from Azure services (like Blob Storage or Resource Manager) and custom sources. Event Grid delivers events to subscribers with low latency and high reliability.

terms.definition: The service that generates an event, such as Azure Storage or a custom app.
An endpoint where events are published. Event Grid topics can be system topics (from Azure) or custom topics.
A filter and endpoint configuration that tells Event Grid where to send matching events.
The destination that receives events, such as an Azure Function, webhook, or Logic App.

data.title: Create an Event Grid Custom Topic (Azure CLI)
data.content: Create a custom topic that your application can publish events to:
data.code:
az eventgrid topic create \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --name myCustomTopic \
  --location eastus \
  --input-schema eventdataschema

data.title: How Event Grid Handles Failures
items: Event Grid retries delivery for up to 24 hours for dead-lettering destinations.
Retries use exponential backoff to reduce pressure on struggling handlers.
Events are stored durably and survive regional outages within the retention window.
You can configure dead-lettering to an Azure Storage blob for undelivered events.

data.title: Event Grid vs. Service Bus
data.text: Event Grid is for reacting to events (fire-and-forget). Service Bus is for reliable messaging with ordering and transactions. Use Event Grid when you need many subscribers to react to the same event; use Service Bus when each message should be processed exactly once.

data.title: React to a Blob Upload
data.description: Set up an Event Grid subscription that triggers a function when a new image is uploaded to a storage container.
steps: Create an Azure Storage container named uploads.
Create an Event Grid system topic for the storage account.
Subscribe to the Microsoft.Storage.BlobCreated event type.
Set the endpoint to an Azure Function URL.
data.expectedOutcome: Every time a blob is uploaded, Event Grid notifies your function.
